newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast late crude prices fall with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast late crude prices fall with NYMEX.

text.p: Crude prices on the West Coast slid late, in line with a sharp downturn in NYMEX December crude, which expired today and forced West Coast bellwether grade -- Alaska North Slope (ANS) -- to drop 75 cents.
West Coast cash prices came under pressure as December NYMEX fell 73 cents on technical selling, traders said.
The futures weakened spot prices for December WTI, which also shed 75 cents today. ANS diffs remained $2.20 under WTI.
Texaco Inc said late Wednesday its 20-inch California crude line remained under repair after a rupture Tueday.
Texaco said earlier a portion of the line, which links Bakersfield oil fields to refineries in San Francisco, shut automatically but would likely return later today.
The line has a 340,000 barrel-per-day throughput.
A trader of Canadian crude expected levels of exports to the West Coast to remain flat in December, versus November.
And another traded reported selling a significant parcel of Line 63 blended crude at $1.00 over postings, the prevailing market level.

No new deals were reported for heavier grades. Kern River was at flat to 10 cents above posted prices, or around $17.00/10, while Line 63 was assessed 95 cents to $1.05 above postings or $3.20 to $3.00 under December WTI.
